description:
Found by the fz-kdt.127.1 adversarial refutation (2026-09-02, probe K2).
PRE-EXISTING, not a regression: identical at base 172ab21f1 and at
fz-kdt.127.1's head.

REPRODUCER (verbatim; kept at
<scratch>/7a73b83f.../scratchpad/fold127.1/K2_map_capture.fz + .exs):

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(m) do
      fn (n) ->
        case m do
          %{a: v} -> n + v
          _ -> n
        end
      end
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(%{a: 1}), 10))
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(%{a: 0.5}), 10))
  end

Elixir oracle: 12 / 11.0.

MEASURED:

  base 172ab21f1   interp: 12.0 11.0 (WRONG first line)
                   JIT:    abort, fz_unbox_float
                   AOT:    build failure
  head (127.1)     interp: 12.0 11.0 (WRONG first line)
                   JIT:    abort, fz_ref_load_float ExpectedTag
                           { expected: ValueKind(14), found: ValueKind(13) }
                   AOT:    same abort

WHY IT IS NOT 127.1's. fz-kdt.127.1 made the callable axis name the
CONSTRUCTION -- a function plus one sub-predicate per capture, each capture
projected through the ordinary runtime-type projection. It therefore
separates two capture layouts exactly as far as the capture's own axis
separates them, and no further. Here the capture is a MAP, and the map axis
is an ERASING axis (fz-kdt.131's residue): its runtime test is a KIND check,
never the contents, so %{a: int} and %{a: float} project to ONE test. The
two constructions are indistinguishable to any test the callable axis can
build out of them, and the value minted over %{a: 1} reaches the body
grounded for %{a: float}.

The cure is UPSTREAM in the map axis, not in the callable axis: the same
residue reaches through every position a map can sit in, and the capture
position is only where this probe found it. The kinds whose test is a kind
check and whose contents are therefore invisible are maps, binaries,
resources and unnamed structs (127.1's re-homed unit test names exactly that
set). Either those contents become answerable, or a body may not be
specialized on them.

RELATION: sibling of fz-kdt.131 (the surface-coverage law -- an arm's test
is COARSER than the surface its body was compiled for); reached through the
capture position opened up by fz-kdt.127.1. 127.1 is correct to be out of
scope here; this ticket owns the source-level reproducer so it is not lost.
title: A map-typed CAPTURE at two value types answers 12.0 for 12 on interp and aborts on both native doors
